correctness.rationale: Finite-rank truncation gives the upper bound. Nearly maximizing finite output rows give finitely supported tail vectors weakly null in the full l_infinity sum via restriction to its c0-sum, so every compact perturbation gives the matching lower bound. Finite l_p duality proves the numerical formula. The endpoint palette is finite for fixed coefficient lists, hence stabilization and compact=finite rank. The example gives exact two-vertex l_p dual norms and the verified q-power sphere ratio. 3494 finite assertions supplement, but do not replace, the proof.

value.rationale: The finding gives an exact entire-family essential norm, including coefficient cancellation and all Banach exponents, not just compactness. Its endpoint compact=finite-rank rigidity and finite stabilization are structurally stronger than finite-p compactness, while a sharp known-map example exhibits a genuine discontinuity in exponent and cutoff order. The invariant is directly motivated by a new complete qualitative compactness classification and supports further perturbative/operator-algebra questions.
